title: An Overview of Applications of Electron Nanodiffraction to Studying the Structure and Dynamics of Amorphous Solids and Liquids
content: High coherence electron nanodiffraction is well-suited to studying the structure and dynamics of amorphous materials, including both solids and liquids. A small probe size matches the interesting structural length scales from the first coordination shell, which constitutes short-range order, out to the third or fourth coordination shell, which constitutes medium range order. Probing a small volume of material causes the uniform fuzzy rings of wide-area diffraction to break into speckles, each of which arises from some arrangement of atoms that diffracts in a particular direction. High coherence increases the contrast of the speckles, improving the signal-to-background ratio for characterization.
